findings.title: Potential SSRF/Parameter Pollution via Unvalidated `params`
findings.description: This change passes the `params` argument to the underlying request method. While the `requests` library handles URL encoding and sanitization of the `params` data structure itself, passing it explicitly allows for the inclusion of user-controlled data in the query string. If the `url` argument or the `params` dictionary contains untrusted data, it could potentially lead to SSRF or parameter pollution depending on how the final request is constructed and sent, although `requests` generally mitigates basic injection risks. However, it is a potential vector if not handled correctly downstream.
findings.suggestion: Ensure that `url` and `params` are validated on the server side. Do not use user input directly as the `url` without proper sanitization and validation of the domain/hostname. If `params` contains user input, ensure they are properly encoded. The `requests` library itself is robust against many injection attacks, but the integration point is the risk.
